questions.answer: A webinar that explained quite well how to go about

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: everything went smoothly

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They recommend having as many pre-apporvals a possible but since the supply courses that correpsond to any mandatory course you have to take abroad is limited this can be a challenge

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: since Sciences Po student go abroad on their third year I was having classes with second year student despite bieng on my thirs yea myself. This did result incourses a bit bellow my level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I found it to be less focused on critical reflection and more interested in quick answers and a heavy work load consisting of many representations and essays throughout the semester. I found that part challenging and also a bit mind-numbing.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Comparative politics
Political identities in the age of discontent
Democratic theory
Decision-Making Process of the European Union: an insider's view (The)
The Euro, migration and climate change: European challenges and opportunitie

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Political identities in the age of discontent and Democratic Theory were both held by a teacher called Thomas Zicman de Barros who was a remarkable teacher and intellect. Both courses were structured in a way that ensured averyone could follow while still challenging all in the class.

The work burden is high, many assignments during the semester
the academic level is per se not very high
a lot of rational choice if you're on exchange with Dansk og Komparativ Politik (Comparative Politics)
